question: Which two mechanisms can restrict access to an S3 bucket so that requests are only accepted when they originate from within a specific VPC, even if the bucket policy would otherwise be permissive? (Choose two.)

options.A: An S3 bucket policy condition using aws:sourceVpce (or aws:sourceVpc)
options.B: A policy attached to the Gateway VPC endpoint restricting which buckets/actions can be reached through it
options.C: A security group attached directly to the S3 bucket
options.D: A Network ACL rule on the subnet where S3 "lives"

explanation: An S3 bucket policy condition using aws:sourceVpce or aws:sourceVpc enforces that requests must come from the designated VPC endpoint or VPC, and a VPC endpoint policy can restrict which buckets and actions can be accessed through that endpoint.

whyOthersAreWrong.E: Controls DNS resolution behavior, not S3 authorization.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Amazon S3 is a managed regional service that does not reside within a VPC subnet; security groups cannot be attached directly to Amazon S3 buckets.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Network ACLs are stateless and apply to entire subnet CIDR blocks; they cannot dynamically reference instance security groups or maintain stateful connection tracking.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using Amazon VPC.

question: A company wants every new EBS volume created in an AWS account, across all Regions the account uses, to be encrypted automatically, without depending on individual engineers to select an "encrypt" checkbox at launch time.

options.A: Publish a wiki page instructing engineers to always tick the encryption checkbox
options.B: Enable the "EBS encryption by default" account setting in each Region in use (optionally enforced/audited with AWS Config)
options.C: Only encrypt production volumes manually after creation
options.D: Replace all EBS volumes with instance store volumes

explanation: EC2 provides a per-Region account-level setting that forces every newly created EBS volume (and every snapshot copy) to be encrypted automatically, removing reliance on manual action. It must be enabled per Region.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: This option relies on human process and will eventually fail.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Leaves a window of unencrypted data and doesn't scale.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Removes durability and persistence entirely and does not address encryption.

learningObjective: Implement secure architectural controls and access policies with Amazon EC2.

question: A read-heavy web application backed by RDS for MySQL suffers degraded performance during peak traffic because many identical SELECT queries repeatedly hit the database for the same, rarely-changing data.

options.A: Add an ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) layer in front of the database to cache frequent query results
options.B: Increase only the EC2 instance size of the application servers
options.C: Add more NAT Gateways
options.D: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration

explanation: Caching frequent, repeated query results in ElastiCache offloads read pressure from the database, since identical requests can be served from an in-memory cache with sub-millisecond latency instead of re-executing the query.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: This option addresses application-tier compute, not database read pressure.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This option is unrelated to database read performance (NAT handles outbound internet traffic).
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Accelerates S3 uploads and is unrelated to a relational database workload.

learningObjective: Optimize workload throughput and latency using Amazon ElastiCache.

question: A leaderboard feature reads the same small set of frequently requested items from a DynamoDB table extremely often, and the company needs microsecond-level read latency for these hot items without re-architecting the data model.

options.A: Rely on DynamoDB auto scaling of read capacity alone
options.B: Add Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) as an in-memory cache in front of the table
options.C: Simply raise the provisioned RCUs further
options.D: Put a generic ElastiCache Memcached cluster that the application talks to using the S3 API

explanation: DAX is a DynamoDB-compatible, in-memory caching layer purpose-built to sit in front of DynamoDB, delivering microsecond response times for cached reads while requiring only minimal application changes (it's API-compatible with the DynamoDB SDK). Options A and C reduce throttling risk but do not reduce per-request latency to microseconds — they still hit the DynamoDB storage engine.

whyOthersAreWrong.D: This option describes a nonsensical mismatch (Memcached does not speak the S3 API) and would require substantial custom cache-aside logic.
whyOthersAreWrong.A: This approach (Rely on DynamoDB auto scaling of read capacity alone) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This approach (Simply raise the provisioned RCUs further) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.

learningObjective: Optimize workload throughput and latency using Amazon DynamoDB.

question: A real-time multiplayer game backend uses UDP and requires the lowest possible latency plus automatic routing of players to the closest, healthiest regional endpoint globally, with fast failover that doesn't depend on DNS caching/TTL behavior on client devices.

options.A: Route 53 latency-based routing
options.B: AWS Global Accelerator
options.C: Amazon CloudFront
options.D: An ALB configured for cross-zone load balancing

explanation: Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and routes traffic over the AWS global network backbone to the closest healthy endpoint, supports both TCP and UDP, and performs fast failover at the network layer independent of client-side DNS caching. Route 53 failover still depends on DNS resolvers respecting TTLs, which can delay failover.

whyOthersAreWrong.C: CloudFront is an HTTP(S) content delivery service and does not support arbitrary UDP game traffic.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: An ALB alone is Regional and does not provide global anycast routing or automatic nearest-endpoint selection.
whyOthersAreWrong.A: DNS-based routing decisions depend on client DNS resolvers honoring record TTLs and cannot react instantaneously to granular Availability Zone health degradations.

learningObjective: Optimize workload throughput and latency using Amazon Route 53.

question: A company's Aurora MySQL development/test database is only used during business hours on weekdays and sits idle the rest of the time. The team wants to minimize cost during idle periods without writing manual start/stop automation.

options.A: Run a fixed-size, always-on provisioned Aurora instance
options.B: Use Aurora Serverless v2, which automatically scales database capacity based on demand, reducing capacity (and cost) during idle periods
options.C: Purchase a Reserved Instance sized for peak dev/test load
options.D: Move the database off AWS to an on-premises server

explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 automatically and near-instantly adjusts database capacity (in fine-grained ACU increments) up or down based on actual demand, so cost drops automatically during nights/weekends when the dev/test database is idle, with no custom scheduling logic required.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: Pays for peak-sized capacity around the clock regardless of use.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Commits to a fixed size for a workload that is explicitly variable, working against cost optimization.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Removes AWS's managed database benefits entirely and isn't a scaling solution.

learningObjective: Select the most cost-effective architecture using Amazon Aurora to satisfy workload requirements.

question: A company runs a mix of workloads across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda, with instance families and Regions that shift over time as needs evolve. It wants a single flexible, commitment-based discount that automatically applies across these compute types in exchange for a 1- or 3-year $/hour spend commitment.

options.A: Standard Reserved Instances
options.B: Compute Savings Plans
options.C: Spot Instances
options.D: Scheduled Reserved Instances

explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply automatically to usage across EC2 (any instance family/size/Region/OS/tenancy), AWS Fargate, and Lambda, up to the committed hourly spend — offering the flexibility this mixed, evolving compute footprint needs. Standard Reserved Instances are tied to a specific instance family and Region (with limited flexibility even with convertible RIs) and don't cover Fargate/Lambda. Spot provides no guaranteed capacity or commitment-based discount model. Scheduled Reserved Instances address recurring, predictable time-windows of capacity, not a general flexible compute discount.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: This approach (Standard Reserved Instances) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This approach (Spot Instances) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: This approach (Scheduled Reserved Instances) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using Amazon EC2.

question: A fault-tolerant batch analytics job can be interrupted and resumed at any point and needs to run at the lowest possible EC2 compute cost.

options.A: On-Demand Instances
options.B: Spot Instances
options.C: Standard Reserved Instances
options.D: Dedicated Instances

explanation: Spot Instances offer the deepest discount (often up to ~90% off On-Demand) by using AWS's spare capacity, in exchange for the possibility of interruption with a two-minute warning — an ideal fit for fault-tolerant, resumable, non-time-critical batch workloads.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: On-Demand and Reserved Instances cost significantly more for this use case and RIs add an unnecessary long-term commitment for a workload that doesn't need guaranteed capacity. Dedicated Instances are for compliance/licensing needs on isolated hardware, at a higher cost, unrelated to this scenario.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: On-Demand and Reserved Instances cost significantly more for this use case and RIs add an unnecessary long-term commitment for a workload that doesn't need guaranteed capacity.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: This approach (Dedicated Instances) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.

learningObjective: Select the most cost-effective architecture using Amazon EC2 to satisfy workload requirements.

question: A security team wants continuous, automated detection of suspicious activity across AWS accounts — such as API calls from unusual geolocations, credentials showing signs of compromise, and EC2 instances that appear to be mining cryptocurrency — without deploying any agents.

options.A: AWS Config
options.B: Amazon GuardDuty
options.C: AWS Trusted Advisor
options.D: Amazon Inspector

explanation: GuardDuty is a managed threat detection service that continuously analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs using threat intelligence and machine learning to surface exactly this class of finding (anomalous API activity, compromised credentials, cryptocurrency-mining behavior) with no agents required. AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance, not threat detection. Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks across cost/performance/security/fault tolerance, not behavioral threat detection. Inspector performs vulnerability assessment of EC2/ECR/Lambda workloads, not account-activity threat detection.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: AWS Config is a detective control that detects and remediates non-compliance asynchronously after resources are created, failing preventive enforcement requirements.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This approach (AWS Trusted Advisor) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: This approach (Amazon Inspector) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using Amazon EC2.

question: A company needs to give a third-party auditor temporary, read-only access to specific S3 buckets for the next 5 days, without creating a permanent IAM user or sharing long-term credentials.

options.A: Create an IAM user with access keys and delete the user after 5 days
options.B: Create an IAM role with a trust policy allowing the auditor's AWS account to assume it via AWS STS, scoped to read-only S3 permissions with a short maximum session duration
options.C: Share the AWS account root user credentials temporarily
options.D: Add a bucket ACL granting read access to "Authenticated Users"

explanation: A cross-account IAM role assumed via STS provides short-lived, automatically expiring temporary credentials scoped to exactly the permissions needed, with no long-term secret to revoke or rotate afterward.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: This configuration creates standing credentials that must be manually deleted and could leak in the meantime.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This approach is a severe security anti-pattern.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: "Authenticated Users" in S3 ACLs actually means any AWS account holder globally, not just the auditor — far too broad.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using AWS IAM.

question: A company needs automated, point-in-time recoverable backups for its RDS database with a configurable retention period, without manually scheduling and managing snapshot jobs.

options.A: Manual, ad hoc snapshots taken by an engineer whenever they remember
options.B: Enable RDS automated backups with a defined retention period, which also enables point-in-time restore
options.C: Manually snapshot the underlying EBS volumes
options.D: Export the database to S3 nightly via a custom cron job

explanation: RDS automated backups take a daily full snapshot plus continuously capture transaction logs, enabling restore to any point in time within the retention window (up to 35 days), fully managed with no custom scheduling logic required.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: This option is manual, inconsistent, and does not enable point-in-time restore.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Bypasses RDS's consistent backup mechanism and application-level consistency guarantees.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: This approach is a custom-built process with significant operational overhead that RDS already provides natively.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using Amazon S3.

question: A production workload runs on EC2 with steady, predictable utilization 24/7, and the company can commit to that usage for the next 3 years in exchange for the lowest possible cost.

options.A: On-Demand Instances
options.B: A 3-year Reserved Instance (or equivalent Compute Savings Plan) commitment
options.C: Spot Instances
options.D: Dedicated Hosts

explanation: For steady-state, predictable, long-running workloads, a 3-year commitment (Reserved Instances or a Compute Savings Plan) delivers the deepest discount versus On-Demand — often up to ~60-70%+ depending on payment option — because AWS trades a usage guarantee for a lower rate. On-Demand offers no discount for guaranteed usage. Spot is unsuitable for workloads that must run continuously without interruption tolerance. Dedicated Hosts address licensing/compliance needs tied to physical server visibility, at a cost premium, and are not chosen purely for steady-state cost savings.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: This approach (On-Demand Instances) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This approach (Spot Instances) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: This approach (Dedicated Hosts) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.

learningObjective: Select the most cost-effective architecture using Amazon EC2 to satisfy workload requirements.

question: A clickstream analytics pipeline must ingest millions of events per second in near real time, preserve per-key (e.g., per-user) ordering, support multiple independent consumers reading the same data, and allow replay of recent data if a consumer needs to reprocess it.

options.A: Amazon SQS Standard queue
options.B: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
options.C: Amazon SNS topic
options.D: DynamoDB Streams from an unrelated table

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams is purpose-built for high-throughput, ordered (per-shard/partition-key) streaming ingestion, supports multiple independent consumer applications reading the same stream concurrently, and retains data for a configurable window (up to 365 days) enabling replay.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: SQS Standard does not guarantee ordering and each message is generally consumed once (not fanned out to multiple independent readers without extra plumbing). SNS fans out but doesn't provide durable, replayable, ordered storage of the stream.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: This option is unrelated to this clickstream data source.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This approach (Amazon SNS topic) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using Amazon Kinesis.

question: An order-processing Lambda function occasionally fails because a downstream third-party API is intermittently unavailable. The company must not lose customer orders during these outages and wants failed messages captured for later inspection.

options.A: Invoke the Lambda function synchronously with no retry or buffering
options.B: Insert an SQS queue between the event source and the Lambda function as a durable buffer, and configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for messages that repeatedly fail processing
options.C: Silently drop failed orders
options.D: Only increase the Lambda function's timeout setting

explanation: Buffering through SQS decouples order ingestion from downstream API availability — messages persist safely in the queue until the Lambda function can process them (with automatic retries), and a DLQ captures messages that exceed the maximum receive count for later investigation without losing them.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: This approach has no resilience to downstream failures and orders are lost on error.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This option is unacceptable for a business-critical workflow.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: This option does not address failures caused by an unavailable downstream dependency — a longer timeout doesn't fix that the API is down.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using Amazon SQS.

question: A tightly-coupled distributed computing workload on EC2 requires sustained network throughput in the tens of Gbps between instances in the same cluster placement group.

options.A: Rely on default (non-enhanced) networking on a small general-purpose instance type
options.B: Choose instance types/sizes that support Enhanced Networking (ENA) with high network bandwidth, combined with a cluster placement group
options.C: Use paravirtual (classic) networking
options.D: Route inter-instance traffic through a NAT Gateway

explanation: Enhanced Networking (via the Elastic Network Adapter) on appropriately sized instance types delivers higher bandwidth, higher packet-per-second performance, and lower inter-instance latency and jitter, and combining it with a cluster placement group maximizes throughput between instances on the same low-latency network fabric.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: Caps achievable throughput well below what's required.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: Paravirtual is a legacy networking type with materially lower performance and isn't available on current-generation Nitro instance types.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Would add unnecessary latency and is not how instances within the same VPC/AZ should communicate with each other.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using Amazon EC2.

question: A regulated company stores large volumes of data across hundreds of S3 buckets and must automatically discover and classify sensitive data such as PII and financial information at scale.

options.A: Amazon Macie
options.B: AWS Config
options.C: Amazon Inspector
options.D: AWS Artifact

explanation: Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching specifically to discover, classify, and report on sensitive data (PII, credentials, financial data) stored in S3 at scale. Config evaluates resource configuration, not data content. Inspector scans compute workloads for software vulnerabilities, not data sensitivity. Artifact is a portal for compliance reports/agreements, not a scanning tool.

whyOthersAreWrong.B: AWS Config is a detective control that detects and remediates non-compliance asynchronously after resources are created, failing preventive enforcement requirements.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This approach (Amazon Inspector) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: This approach (AWS Artifact) fails to satisfy the scenario constraints with the required operational efficiency, cost effectiveness, or security controls.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using Amazon S3.

question: A significant portion of a company's monthly bill comes from NAT Gateway data processing charges for private-subnet traffic destined to Amazon S3. The company wants to eliminate this specific cost without changing where instances are deployed.

options.A: Add more NAT Gateways for redundancy
options.B: Add a Gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and update the private subnets' route tables so S3-bound traffic no longer traverses the NAT Gateway
options.C: Move the instances into public subnets
options.D: Increase the NAT Gateway's provisioned bandwidth

explanation: A Gateway VPC endpoint for S3 is free of charge and, once the route table is updated, S3-bound traffic from the private subnet routes directly to S3 over the AWS network instead of through the NAT Gateway — eliminating both the NAT data processing charge and the extra network hop for that traffic.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: This option increases cost without addressing the root cause.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This configuration exposes instances to the internet and doesn't reduce cost as intended (it also changes the deployment model, which the requirement rules out).
whyOthersAreWrong.D: (NAT Gateways don't have a manually provisioned bandwidth setting) would not reduce per-GB processing charges regardless.

learningObjective: Select the most cost-effective architecture using Amazon VPC to satisfy workload requirements.

question: A single event (e.g., "order placed") must trigger multiple independent downstream systems — sending a confirmation email, sending an SMS, and loading a record into a data warehouse pipeline — reliably and in parallel.

options.A: Use a single SQS FIFO queue with one consumer processing all three tasks sequentially
options.B: Publish once to an SNS topic with multiple subscribed endpoints/SQS queues (fan-out pattern)
options.C: Chain the three systems together with direct synchronous Lambda invocations
options.D: Have three unrelated polling loops all read from one shared queue and race to process the message

explanation: The SNS fan-out pattern publishes a message once and delivers a copy to every subscribed endpoint (which can be separate SQS queues, Lambda functions, email, SMS, etc.) in parallel and independently — a failure or delay in one subscriber does not affect delivery to the others.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: Serializes the three tasks and couples them to a single consumer's logic.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This configuration creates a fragile, tightly-coupled synchronous chain.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: Risks duplicate processing and unpredictable ordering with no isolation between the three downstream systems.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using Amazon SQS.

question: A globally distributed application uses DynamoDB and must remain available and writable in multiple Regions simultaneously, surviving the loss of any single Region, with AWS-managed conflict resolution for concurrent writes to the same item.

options.A: Take on-demand backups and copy them to a second Region manually
options.B: Enable DynamoDB Global Tables across the required Regions
options.C: Configure DynamoDB "cross-region read replicas" (not an actual DynamoDB feature)
options.D: Use Aurora Global Database instead

explanation: DynamoDB Global Tables provide fully managed, multi-Region, multi-active replication with last-writer-wins conflict resolution, so applications can read and write in any participating Region and the table remains available even if a Region is lost.

whyOthersAreWrong.A: This approach is a manual, non-continuous process unsuitable for active-active needs.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This option describes a feature DynamoDB does not have (this pattern is achieved specifically through Global Tables).
whyOthersAreWrong.D: This approach is a relational database service, not a substitute for a DynamoDB-based design.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using Amazon Aurora.

question: An application in a private subnet must be able to initiate outbound HTTPS connections to download OS security patches, but must never accept any inbound connection initiated from the internet. What should be added to the VPC design?

options.A: Attach an Internet Gateway directly to the private subnet's route table
options.B: Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet and add a default route from the private subnet to it
options.C: Assign an Elastic IP directly to each private instance
options.D: Create a VPC peering connection to a separate public-facing VPC

explanation: A NAT Gateway, placed in a public subnet with a route to the Internet Gateway, allows instances in private subnets to initiate outbound connections while making it impossible for hosts on the internet to initiate inbound connections to those private instances (NAT only translates and forwards traffic that originated from inside the VPC).

whyOthersAreWrong.A: Would make the subnet public and expose instances directly.
whyOthersAreWrong.C: This approach requires public IPs on the private instances, defeating the design.
whyOthersAreWrong.D: This option does not provide internet access at all.

learningObjective: Architect a reliable and scalable cloud solution using Amazon VPC.
